rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Nepal conserves about a quarter of its land in a protected-area network — 12 national parks (Chitwan, Bardia, Sagarmatha, Langtang), a wildlife reserve (Koshi Tappu with its wild water buffalo), Dhorpatan Hunting Reserve, six community-managed conservation areas (Annapurna, Kanchenjunga) and 13 buffer zones that share park benefits with local people.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
A national park is managed for wildlife and visitors, and people do not live in the core. Chitwan, gazetted in 1973, was Nepal's first.
Sagarmatha National Park protects the Everest region and is also a World Heritage site.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **National park vs conservation area:** parks are strictly protected with no consumptive use; conservation areas are community-managed with sustainable use.  ·  **Buffer zone vs core zone:** the core is strictly protected; the buffer fringe shares benefits with local communities to reduce pressure and conflict.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** Name the only hunting reserve of Nepal and its target species. **Answer.** **Dhorpatan Hunting Reserve** (western Nepal) — the country's only hunting reserve, where **regulated hunting of blue sheep** (*Pseudois nayaur*) and a few other species is permitted under licence, with revenue funding conservation.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Buffer zones turn conflict into partnership:** revenue sharing makes conservation pay local communities — the social innovation behind Nepal's conservation success.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Nepal's network: 12 national parks, 1 wildlife reserve (Koshi Tappu), 1 hunting reserve (Dhorpatan), 6 conservation areas, 13 buffer zones — ~24% of the country.  ·  Hotspots: exceptional endemism + ≥70% habitat loss; Nepal lies in the Himalaya hotspot (and Indo-Burma edge).  ·  Ramsar wetlands (9): Bishazari Tal, Ghodaghodi Tal, Jagadishpur, Koshi Tappu, Gosaikunda, Rara, Mai Pokhari, Phoksundo, Gokyo.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Sagarmatha National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — the park protecting Everest's slopes.
